rapport_notes: Brianne is warm, conversational, uses the customer's name, recovers well from word-fumbles ("freight that you can or order deliver"), and maintains genuine engagement throughout.
process_discipline_notes: No silence held after the agenda question — rep launches immediately into packing logistics. No silence held after the final offer — rep ends with "reply to the email and we'll get you on the books" without waiting for customer response or explicit close confirmation.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: I'll start with a few questions to get us on the right track and then that should take about six minutes and then I'll be able to build you an accurate quote
evidence_quotes.agenda: do you have any specific questions or concerns you'd like answered on this call?
evidence_quotes.agenda_response: Just the, I was curious about packing and like unpacking services and, and like what is, what the cost about it?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep_gap: Rep asks "Are we gonna want the whole house packed or just the kitchen?" Customer says "Yes, the whole." Rep responds "Oh, the whole shebang" and pivots to Einstein differentiators — no second layer follow-up on the packing cost concern the customer raised.

So, it's not like they're just gonna pack, they'll use if they pack in four hours and we estimated six they'll use those two hours to kind of prep for the next day and then obviously time comes off of your move

top_strength: Brianne nailed the quid pro quo framing and asked the customer's agenda before diving into logistics — she also covered all three Stage 2 differentiators early (damage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time) and delivered a thorough estimate with anchoring and personalization.
coaching_note: Follow up two layers deep on every customer concern raised — when David asked about packing costs, ask "What else are you wondering about packing?" before moving on; also hold silence after the agenda question and after your final offer to give the customer room to respond naturally rather than filling the space.
